transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-03-13 14:00 UTC | Duration: 45 min | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (Atlas CTO), Ben (Atlas SRE), Anika (Product), Ravi (Eng)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick check — can we do roll call?
[00:05] Marta: Marta here.
[00:06] Ben: Ben here.
[00:08] Anika: Anika.
[00:10] Ravi: Ravi.
[00:12] Jordan: great. Priya on the line too?
[00:13] Priya: yep, hi all. I'll run through the incident summary then we can go into the tuning items.

[00:30] Priya: recap — on 2026-03-11 at ~16:12 UTC you hit a sustained wave of 5xxs and timeouts for about 18 minutes, most errors were 503 and a few 504 timeouts. We saw retries from your client end spike which caused token amplification and backpressure.
[00:50] Ben: yeah we saw the alerts; our dashboard showed a simultaneous CPU spike on the inference fleet and queue depth grew. some requests had 3x retry loops before success.
[00:58] Jordan: to be clear, the path was through the hosted API not the Dedicated pilot, correct?
[01:03] Ben: correct, hosted for the trial.
[01:06] Priya: right — root cause looks like twofold: transient worker oom on one of the autoscaled clusters and an unexpected request pattern that serialized longer sequences than the median leading to kernel contention. Also an internal rate limiter configuration briefly misfired during the pod reschedule so tokens were being dropped and clients retried.
[01:30] Marta: can you explain the "kernel contention" bit?
[01:33] Priya: sure — on long sequences the runtime picks a different attention kernel path; when many of those align it pushes memory and scheduling, and if a node gets OOM it causes some requests to fail fast with 503 while the autoscaler spins up replacement pods. because of prefix caching misses we saw higher overall token work.
[01:50] Ravi: you mean K-V cache? I thought the pilot had prefix cache enabled.
[01:53] Priya: yes, we did have KV cache enabled but there were some misses — possibly because the request distribution changed. also I miss-typed earlier in the ticket as "K-V cash" sorry, transcription note.

[02:10] Jordan: from a mitigation standpoint we did: hotfix 1) bump max worker count in the pool, 2) adjust the internal rate-limiter to return 429s with Retry-After for aggressive clients instead of dropping, and 3) apply a rolling restart to clear the OOM state. that reduced errors within 7 minutes.
[02:30] Ben: we noticed error volume drop after the restart, yes. we still saw occasional 5xxs for high seq length batches.
[02:36] Priya: next step recommended is to tune client retry/backoff. we suggested exponential backoff w/ jitter and max retries 2 for non-idempotent generation calls; also circuit-breakers on client side to avoid retry storms.
[02:50] Anika: our SDK default had 5 retries, that was probably the problem.
[02:54] Jordan: yep that amplifies. Also we want to propose two infra options: keep hosted but apply a policy change (reserved burst capacity + kernel-level queue prioritization) OR move to Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput. price vs reliability tradeoff.
[03:12] Marta: what's the expected throughput delta if we go Dedicated?
[03:15] Priya: Dedicated gives you guaranteed GPU pools; for similar instance types you'll see lower P99 latency and fewer scheduling events — practically you avoid multi-tenant pressure. For your observed peak of ~180 rps with many medium-length sequences, Dedicated sized to 2 nodes is a conservative baseline.
[03:35] Ben: any quick win for hosted to prevent recurrence?
[03:38] Priya: yes: 1) reduce client retries to 2 + exponential backoff with full jitter, 2) apply request-level token quotas at your edge to smooth bursts, 3) enable server-side prefix caching warmup for the common prompt templates, 4) enable early rejection with 429 and Retry-After so clients back off. we can push a config change for 3 and 4 on your pilot cluster.
[04:05] Jordan: I'm going to drop links in the followup: the incident timeline, a benchmark spreadsheet, and the runbook.
[04:12] Ben: please include logs where possible — we will correlate with our SRE traces.

[04:30] Priya: small note — there was a misconfiguration in the autoscaler threshold (it was tuned to CPU rather than GPU mem pressure for this model) so scaling lagged. fixed that in the hotfix.
[04:45] Ravi: are there any changes to model selection / quantization that could reduce memory pressure?
[04:50] Priya: yes, we recommended a quantized variant (8-bit) for lower memory and CPU kernel usage; tradeoff is slight delta on generation quality. Redwood Optimize has a profile that estimates p95 latency and token cost difference; I'll attach the profile.
[05:10] Marta: quality is important for us — we need to see A/B results before switching. can Redwood run a small quality regression?
[05:15] Priya: we can — we have your eval harness from earlier; suggest we run 500 prompt pairs across baseline and quantized model and share the metrics.

[05:30] Jordan: ok, let's go through timeline/outcomes — Priya do you want to read the RCA bullets?
[05:34] Priya: sure. RCA bullets: 1) spike in high-length requests + client retry amplification, 2) autoscaler threshold was using CPU signal not GPU mem causing delayed scale, 3) transient worker OOM leading to 503s, 4) rate limiter misconfiguration dropped requests instead of returning 429 causing retries. Remediation: applied rolling restart, increased pool limits, fixed rate limiter to return 429+Retry-After, updated autoscaler, and added short term Dedicated-like burst capacity for pilot.
[06:05] Ben: sounds right. how do we validate that the fix is effective?
[06:09] Priya: we recommend two validation steps: 1) synthetic benchmark (10k requests at your traffic profile), 2) steady-state soak test for 30 min at 1.5x expected peak. we provided a benchmark script link in the deck.
[06:25] Anika: will your suggested client config be in a patch for our SDK?
[06:28] Jordan: yes, we plan to ship a small SDK patch and config snippet. I'll include it in the email.

[06:40] Marta: about observability — can we get token-level cost and p99 traces for the pilot?
[06:44] Priya: yes, Redwood Console already has token-level breakdown we can share a dashboard link to; we'll give you a 14-day extended retention for the pilot logs.
[06:55] Ravi: security question — did the incident impact any logs with PII or require anything from compliance?
[06:59] Priya: no customer data was exfiltrated, traffic was transiently failed; we'll include audit logs in the incident packet. also we can share SOC2 artifact references if you need.

[07:15] Ben: what about throttling at edge — do you recommend we do a per-user qps cap?
[07:19] Jordan: yes per-user qps cap with token bucket smoothing is recommended; it prevents hot keys from saturating the cluster.

[07:35] Priya: we also want to propose a short pilot extension to validate Dedicated sizing if the benchmark shows >200rps sustained. this gives time to provision dedicated nodes and run a deterministic test.
[07:50] Marta: okay tentatively agree — we need the RCA doc first to present to procurement.

[08:05] Jordan: recap of next steps — Priya uploads RCA + timeline by Monday (2026-03-15), Jordan shares Dedicated pricing and pilot extension proposal, Ben runs benchmarks and uploads logs by 2026-03-20, SE to send SDK patch and recommended client retry config.
[08:30] Anika: one more ask — can you add a short FAQ for our support team about interpreting 429 vs 503?
[08:34] Priya: will do, short one-pager.

[08:50] Jordan: cool, we'll follow up via email with links: incident timeline, benchmark spreadsheet, runbook, Dedicated pricing. thanks everyone.
[08:58] Marta: thanks.
[09:00] Meeting end.
